The CPU (processor) is the general-purpose brain; the GPU (graphics card) is a specialist that is much faster at the kind of number-crunching the linker does. GPU mode is faster, but needs memory.

How many paragraphs the linker processes at the same time. Bigger batch = faster, but uses more memory. Adjustable in Settings → Performance.
If your graphics card hits 86°C, the linker automatically pauses heavy work until it cools back down to 78°C. This protects the hardware.

DARB: Boosts pages from highly-trusted sites that barely link out, so their authority does not get lost in dead-end pages. Source: FR-099 spec.
KMIG: Adds a small bonus to suggested links that introduce a fresh topic the host page has not covered yet. Source: FR-100 spec.
TAPB: Boosts pages that act as the only bridge between two parts of the site so they stay reachable. Source: FR-101 spec.
KCIB: Boosts pages that sit deep inside a dense cluster of related pages (well-integrated content). Source: FR-102 spec.
BERP: Slightly penalises suggestions that would pile yet another link across an already-over-used bridge between page clusters. Source: FR-103 spec.
HGTE: Boosts host pages that touch many different topics, so suggestions for those hosts stay diverse instead of repetitive. Source: FR-104 spec.
RSQVA: Aligns suggestions with the actual Google-search vocabulary your readers use, so links match what real visitors are searching for. Source: FR-105 spec.

Add complementary candidate retrievers to Stage-1. The semantic (BGE-M3 cosine) retriever is always on. Flipping either flag below activates Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF, pick #31) per destination. Source: Cormack et al. 2009 SIGIR.
Group C.2 — adds the LexicalRetriever (token-overlap on titles + scopes). Catches synonyms / spelling-out gaps that dense embeddings miss.

Group C.3 — adds the QueryExpansionRetriever (Rocchio 1971 / Lavrenko-Croft 2001 PRF). Pulls in hosts that share expansion terms even when they don't share literal title tokens. Combine with lexical retriever for the richest fused ranking.
XenForo BM25 retriever (Enhanced Search via REST API)

Adds the XenForoBM25Retriever (Path A). For each destination, queries XenForo's Enhanced Search (Elasticsearch-backed BM25) via the existing API key and contributes BM25-ranked forum candidates. Fused with FAISS via RRF. XF-source candidates only — WordPress / blog / crawled hosts are unaffected. Source: docs/specs/xf-bm25-retrieval.md, BM25 Robertson & Zaragoza 2009.
